about_blocks.text: Ketamine-assisted psychotherapy on the Hamilton Mountain

Field Trip Health Hamilton is a weekday outpatient clinic in the Eastmount neighbourhood, up on the Hamilton Mountain at 688 Queensdale Avenue East. It offers ketamine-assisted psychotherapy to adults with depression, anxiety, PTSD, OCD, chronic pain or substance use problems, most of whom have already tried medication or talk therapy without enough relief.

about_blocks.text: The unit is on the ground floor, right across from a pharmacy entrance, with free parking outside. People come from across Hamilton and from Burlington, Ancaster, Dundas and the Niagara towns. The clinic works under the Field Trip Health Canada name and says it works closely with veterans, first responders, healthcare workers and Indigenous communities.

about_blocks.text: You can't book a dosing session straight away. First comes a free 15-minute call with the care team, then a health questionnaire and a 50-minute medical consultation with a nurse practitioner. That consult has a fee, since OHIP does not pay for it, and it is where the decision about eligibility gets made. Some health problems rule the treatment out, including pregnancy, a personal history of psychosis, uncontrolled hypertension and a recent serious head injury.

about_blocks.text: People who go ahead usually follow a plan of 6 or 9 dosing sessions. On those days a nurse gives the medicine, mostly as an intramuscular injection, and your therapist stays in the room for the whole session, which runs about two and a half hours. Between sessions you meet the same therapist to work through what happened.

about_blocks.text: The Hamilton therapists are mainly registered social workers and registered psychotherapists, and one, Selina Buesink, is also a registered Canadian art therapist (RCAT). Besides the psychedelic program, the clinic offers individual therapy, pain management and stellate ganglion block. It does not provide MDMA or psilocybin therapy, and it describes the treatment as one option inside a wider care plan rather than a cure.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Field Trip Health Hamilton

faqs.question: Does Field Trip Health Hamilton offer residential treatment or detox?

answer_blocks.text: No. The Hamilton clinic is outpatient only, open on weekdays, and you leave after each appointment. It has no beds and does not do withdrawal management. People who need a live-in program or detox should ask about other options on the discovery call or compare residential centres in Hamilton, Niagara and the rest of Ontario.

faqs.question: What conditions are treated at the Hamilton clinic?

answer_blocks.text: Field Trip Health Hamilton uses ketamine-assisted psychotherapy mostly for depression, anxiety, PTSD, OCD, addiction and chronic pain. Its therapists also work with grief, ADHD, bipolar disorder, eating disorders, complex PTSD and relationship problems. The clinic presents the treatment as one part of a broader plan, often for people who have tried several standard treatments.

faqs.question: What does treatment in Hamilton cost?

answer_blocks.text: Prices are not published online; the total depends on the number of sessions in your plan and how the medicine is given, and the team goes through it on a free discovery call. The 50-minute nurse practitioner consultation is not covered by OHIP. Many clients put psychotherapy or nursing benefits from their extended health plan toward part of the cost, and financing through outside lenders is available.

faqs.question: How long are sessions and how many are there?

answer_blocks.text: A session at the Hamilton clinic lasts about 2.5 hours, which covers preparation, the medicine and some integration time. Standard plans include 6 or 9 dosing sessions, with talk therapy appointments in between. Once the core sessions are done, you and the team decide on any ongoing care.

faqs.question: Who is not eligible for psychedelic-assisted therapy?

answer_blocks.text: A nurse practitioner makes the final call in a medical consultation. The clinic lists an allergy to the medicine, pregnancy, a personal history of schizophrenia or psychosis, uncontrolled high blood pressure and a recent severe head injury as reasons it may not be suitable. Your current medications are reviewed in the same appointment.

faqs.question: Where exactly is the clinic, and is there parking?

answer_blocks.text: The address is 688 Queensdale Avenue East, Unit 1A, Hamilton, on the Mountain in the Eastmount area. Once inside the building, the clinic is the first unit on your left, across from the pharmacy entrance. Parking is free on site, several HSR bus stops are a short walk away, and you can reach it by bus from the Hamilton GO Centre.

faqs.question: Do I need a doctor to refer me?

answer_blocks.text: No. You can book the free discovery call yourself. Family doctors and other clinicians can also send a referral using Field Trip Health's referral form or the Ocean eReferral network.

faqs.question: Is the Hamilton clinic still operating, and who runs it?

answer_blocks.text: Yes. The clinic's page on fieldtriphealth.ca listed its address, hours and team in October 2026, and it takes bookings under the Field Trip Health Canada name. The Canadian clinics were taken over by the Canadian Centre for Psychedelic Healing after the original company's 2023 restructuring, so the US fieldtriphealth.com site is not the one to use.
